
### Decidability for the Notes of the Unit 2 - Regular Expressions and Languages in the Theory of Automata and Formal Languages

* Decidability is the ability to determine whether a problem can be solved in a finite amount of time and space.
* Regular expressions are a set of symbols that are used to describe a pattern that can be used to match strings of characters.
* Languages are sets of strings of characters that can be generated by a grammar.
* Automata are machines that can recognize and generate languages.
* Formal languages are languages that are defined by a set of rules.
* Decidability is important in the study of automata and formal languages because it allows us to determine whether a given problem can be solved in a finite amount of time and space.
* Decidability is used to determine whether a given string is a member of a language, or whether a given grammar generates a given language.
* Decidability can also be used to determine whether a given language is regular or context-free.
